newsitem.title: TUNISIA: TUNISIA, KUWAIT SIGN $10.5 MLN OIL PIPELINE DEAL.
newsitem.headline: TUNISIA, KUWAIT SIGN $10.5 MLN OIL PIPELINE DEAL.

text.p: Tunisia on Thursday signed a $10.5 million deal with Kuwait to build an oil pipeline linking Sidi Kilani oilfield to the southern port of La Skhira, the official TAP news agency said.
The pipeline project, worth 12.2 million dinars ($10.5 million), will be built on eleven-month period with a capacity of 25,000 barrels per day, TAP said.
Tunisian Petroleum and Industrial Realisation Contractor (PIRECO) and Kuwait Foreign Petroleum Exploration Co (KUFPEC) were involved in the 125 km pipeline project, the agency said.
KUFPEC owns 45 percent of Sidi Kilani oilfield, which is the third largest oilfield in Tunisia. Its output reached 800,000 tonnes in 1996, or 17,000 barrels per day, industry sources said.
The signing ceremony was attended by Industry Minister Slaheddine Bouguerra and visiting Kuwaiti Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi.
